evidence.summary: renew(subscription, create_order) returns create_order(subscription['customer'], subscription['price']): a renewal creates one order through an injected callback.
The user describes Subscribe as monthly subscriptions that create orders.

database: none: subscriptions are dicts passed in by the caller

architecture.backend: One free function; order creation is injected as a callback, so it is already decoupled from the order store.

features.name: Renew a subscription into an order
features.description: Each renewal of a subscription creates a new order for the subscription's customer at the subscription's price.
features.observed_behaviour: renew() calls create_order(customer, price) and returns its result. It does not charge, schedule or record the renewal.
features.business_logic: Price is copied from the subscription at renewal time. No billing period, no schedule and no guard against renewing the same period twice are in the code; 'monthly' comes only from the user's description.
features.integration: Needs an order-creation function (customer, amount) -> order.

rules.value: monthly (documented by the user, not in code)

unknowns: How renewals are scheduled and how a period is identified: not in the code; only 'monthly' is documented.
Units of subscription['price'] (task.md's create_order takes amount_cents, so cents is assumed for the unified app).
